candidates.subject: The Fish That Fuses With Its Mate
candidates.novelty: Two sexed vertebrates become permanently tissue-connected while remaining distinct organisms.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: Species-specific anatomy and convergent immune gene-loss research support the core; sensory behavior, detailed vasculature and evolutionary reasons qualified.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: In the triplewart seadevil, a male can permanently join a female through fused tissue and vascular connections, gaining nutrition while retaining his reproductive role; reproductive assurance is an evolutionary explanation.
candidates.visualPotential: Tiny male → enormous female → persistent jaw-skin contact → tissue bridge → later vascular join → connected pair.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: How can two adult fish physically join without rejecting one another?
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original deterministic species-informed anatomical animation and local primary narrator.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Selected for the biological mechanism, no aquatic preset or domain whitelist.
candidates.comparison: Owner selected topic; evidence narrows to Cryptopsaras couesii and separates observation from theory.
limitations: Cutaway illustrative and time compressed; no exact vascular map.
Gene losses evolutionary, not a moment-of-bite switch; residual immunity unresolved.
